newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian Chem & Allied Prod restructures.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian Chem & Allied Prod restructures.

text.p: Nigeria's Chemical and Allied Products Plc said on Friday it was cutting 20 percent of its 600-strong workforce in a restructuring to take it into the next century.

The company, which manufactures paints, pharmaceuticals, industrial and agro chemicals, said in a statement to the stock exchange that the affected workers were in ancillary areas with no direct relevance to its core business.

"The exercise will entail re-organisation of functions, rationalisation of old brands and the introduction of new ones with niche marketing potentials," company secretary Deji Okunola said in the statement.
He said the exercise stemmed from the company's bid to re-focus to face anticipated local and global challenges.

"It will also entail heavy investment in the acquisition of local plants identified as capable of ensuring uninterrupted supplies of essential raw materials to core manufacturing outfits," Okunola said.
CAPP is owned 59 percent by private individuals, 40 percent by UAC Nigeria Plc and one percent by employees.

Its shares closed 10 kobo down at 7.70 naira on Friday and traders attributed this to debt problems they said the company was facing. "With luck, it could survive its current troubles and bounce back," one said.
